battle.name: 紅河戰爭
battle.theater: 德克薩斯潘漢德與斯泰克平原
battle.brief: 一八七四年至七五年，美軍在德克薩斯潘漢德草原向南部平原聯盟發動追擊，摧毀其營地、奪走馬匹與皮貨，最終在帕洛杜羅峽谷攻破對方最後的冬季宿營。騎兵縱隊靠快馬與車隊維持機動，加特林機槍則只在營地夜襲與據點防守時發揮火力，追不上連日奔襲的行程。

kit.name: 加特林機槍
kit.history: 六根管子用人力轉動。它的後坐力分散在六次上，所以能壓住一個師。

countries: 這場戰爭的對面只有一方：美利堅合眾國聯邦政府，對手是南部分落的美國原住民族聯盟。聯盟以科曼奇、基奧瓦、南部夏延三支為主，另有少量卡多與阿拉帕霍人一同行動。三支沒有集中的指揮部，也沒有固定編制，各以家族與營帳群為單位推舉頭目，決策靠宿營地上的議事與馬背上的傳令，遇戰則由最有威望的頭目臨時率眾，並隨時把隊伍拆成數十人的小隊在草原上往來游走。他們的武力核心是戰馬，配備則以獵槍、弓矢與長矛為主，其後又從美軍手中繳獲大量步槍與卡賓槍。聯盟的退路同時指向南北兩端：向北可退入阿爾伯塔與加拿大草原，向南則有卡多部落的接應與掩護，使美軍無法同時封住所有去路。聯盟方面的持久能力建立在三樣東西上：能遷徙數百里的馬群、能製成帳篷與冬衣的牛皮，以及在舊營地留下的熟牛肉與乾酪，這三樣也正是美軍後來以遠征方式系統性摧毀的目標。聯盟內部並非鐵板一塊，基奧瓦的薩坦塔力主抵抗到底，科曼奇的基金伯德則傾向接受談判，裂痕最終出現在美軍壓力到來、兩條路線分道揚鑣的時候。
countriesEn: On one side of this war there was a single party: the federal government of the United States. On the other stood a confederation of the Native nations of the Southern Plains. The confederation was made up principally of the Comanche, the Kiowa and the Southern Cheyenne, with a small number of Caddo and Arapaho travelling alongside them. The three nations had no central command and no standing establishment: each raised a council of war among families and tent groups, carried its decisions by mounted messenger, and in battle put the war party under whichever chief commanded the most respect, breaking constantly into bands of a few dozen men who moved back and forth across the grasslands. Their strength at arms rested on the war pony, and their equipment was hunting rifles, bows and lances, later joined by large numbers of muskets and carbines taken from the Americans. Their lines of retreat ran in two directions at once, north toward Alberta and the Canadian prairies, and south to the shelter and succour of the Caddo, so that the army could never seal every outlet at once. The confederation's capacity to keep fighting rested on three things: herds of horses that could travel hundreds of miles, buffalo hides that made tents and winter clothing, and the dried beef and pemmican left behind at the old camps. Those three things were precisely what the army set out to destroy systematically with its long marches. Nor was the confederation of one mind: Satanta of the Kiowa pressed for resistance to the end, while Kicking Bird of the Comanche leaned toward negotiation, and the split finally opened when army pressure arrived and the two courses parted ways.
people: 美軍方面的關鍵人物集中在西部司令部與前線騎兵團兩個層次。菲利普·謝里丹是全戰役的實際統帥，他以西部司令部司令的身分從堪薩斯前進到德克薩斯，決定了一八七四年秋冬季遠征的規模、路線與時間表；下轄的第 1、第 4、第 6、第 7 騎兵團是唯一的機動打擊力量。拉納爾·麥肯齊中校是執行最積極的指揮官，他帶領第 4 騎兵團以連續襲擊摧毀基奧瓦、科曼奇與夏延的村落，被部下稱為最有效率的指揮官；與他搭檔的第 7 騎兵團團長喬治·福賽思在冬季遠征中指揮攜有機關加特林機槍的支隊。印第安事務局與軍隊是兩套並行的系統，代理人之死正是兩者矛盾最尖銳的一次：駐西爾堡的印第安代理人托馬斯·墨菲在一八七四年十一月十三日被基奧瓦人殺害，第 2 騎兵團團長約翰·貝勒隨即搜查附近村落並拘捕三名主犯。聯盟方面值得記住的頭目有三：基奧瓦的薩坦塔在談判時被引入康喬堡而遭絞刑，此後拒絕出席任何集會；科曼奇的基金伯德簽下條約，最後卻被自己人殺死；夏延的夸娜·帕克拒絕進入保留地，率領最後一批自由營帳在草原上堅持到一八七八年。墨菲之死與薩坦塔於一八七八年被自己人殺死這兩件事，說明聯盟內部的信任已經崩解。總統尤利西斯·格蘭特在華盛頓批准遠征與撥款，前線的時間表因此由後方決定。
peopleEn: On the American side the decisive figures sat at two levels, the western department command and the cavalry regiments in the field. Philip Sheridan was the effective commander of the whole war: as commander of the Department of the Gulf he advanced from Kansas into Texas and settled the size, the routes and the timetable of the great expedition of the autumn and winter of 1874, and the 1st, 4th, 6th and 7th Cavalry under him were the only mobile striking force available. Colonel Ranald Mackenzie was the most energetic commander in execution, leading the 4th Cavalry in a series of raids that destroyed the villages of the Kiowa, the Comanche and the Cheyenne, and his own troopers called him the most effective commander they had served under; paired with him, Lieutenant Colonel George Forsyth of the 7th Cavalry commanded the brigade that carried the mounted Gatling guns on the winter march. The Indian Office and the army were two systems running in parallel, and the killing of an agent was the sharpest of their collisions: Thomas Murphy, the Indian agent at Fort Sill, was killed by Kiowa men on 13 November 1874, and Colonel John Baylor of the 2nd Cavalry immediately searched the neighbouring villages and arrested three principals. Three leaders of the confederation deserve to be named: Satanta of the Kiowa was drawn into Fort Cobb under the flag of a council and hanged, after which he refused to attend any meeting; Kicking Bird of the Comanche signed a treaty and was in the end killed by his own people; and Quanah Parker of the Cheyenne refused to enter a reservation, leading the last free band of tents on the plains until 1878. Murphy's death and Satanta's own death at the hand of his people in 1878 together show that trust inside the confederation had collapsed. President Ulysses Grant approved the expedition and the appropriations in Washington, which meant the timetable in the field was set at the rear.
kits: 卡面這件加特林機槍是聯邦軍隊在一八七〇年代最重的幾種武器之一。它在一八六〇年由里查德·加特林取得專利，南北戰爭期間由柯特兵工廠大量生產，戰事結束時仍在軍械庫中大量積壓；西部戰爭沿用的正是這些舊槍，規格為六管、.50 口徑、手搖發射，連同附屬支架、備份槍管與彈藥箱由數匹馬分載，手搖時每分鐘約二百發，柯特曾以蒸汽機演示每分鐘四百發，最遠有效射程接近一千碼，缺點則是笨重、怕沙塵、發射時需要十幾人輪流搖動把柄。遠征軍開拔時把加特林機槍配給騎兵旅的砲兵分隊，作為營地夜襲與據點防守的骨幹火力，使用最密集的一次是一八七五年一月九日西爾堡遭襲的守城戰，以及同年福賽思縱隊冬季推進時的營地掩護。除機關槍外，遠征軍的主武器是一八七三年式春田卡賓槍與一八七三年式後膛步槍，輔以十二磅與六磅野戰炮、三吋野戰炮，砲位由馬匹牽引轉移；物資依靠牛車與四馬篷車輸送，單車載重約二千至三千磅，隨軍品目還包括罐頭牛肉、餅乾、飼料、醫藥與架設軍用電報線的器材。聯盟方面的裝備以戰馬、獵槍、弓矢、長矛與自製皮甲為主，其後則大量使用從美軍手中繳獲的步槍與卡賓槍。兩造在火力上的差距，主要不在槍口，而在馬匹數量與彈藥補充的速度。
kitsEn: The Gatling gun on this card was among the heaviest weapons in the federal army of the 1870s. Richard Gatling patented it in 1860, it was produced in large numbers by the Colt armory during the Civil War, and by the end of that war large stocks of it remained in the arsenals; the Indian Wars fought with those existing guns, of six barrels, .50 calibre, hand-cranked, and they travelled with their mounting, spare barrels and ammunition boxes divided among several horses. Turned by hand they fired about two hundred rounds a minute, and Colt demonstrated four hundred a minute with a steam engine, their useful range reaching close to a thousand yards. The drawbacks were weight, a fear of sand, and the need for a dozen men or more to take turns at the crank. On the march the expedition assigned the Gatling guns to the artillery detachments of the cavalry brigades, as the backbone of camp defence and of fire against a night attack; the densest use came during the defence of Fort Sill on 9 January 1875, and in the covering of the camps during Forsyth's advance the following winter. Apart from the machine guns, the expedition's principal arms were the 1873 pattern Springfield carbines and 1873 pattern Springfield rifles, supported by twelve-pounder and six-pounder field guns and a three-inch gun, all on horse-drawn carriages; supplies moved on ox-carts and four-horse wagons carrying roughly two to three thousand pounds each, and the trains also carried canned beef, hard bread, forage, medical stores and the equipment for stringing military telegraph wire. The confederation's equipment consisted of war ponies, hunting rifles, bows and lances and home-made hide armour, together with large quantities of muskets and carbines captured from American troops. The real gap between the two sides lay not at the muzzle but in the number of horses and in the speed at which ammunition could be replenished.
tactics: 美軍在這一場戰爭裡沒有守住任何陣地的打算，這一點決定了全部戰術。遠征軍由數個旅組成，以大縱隊沿草原平行推進，白天以偵察隊搜索村落方位，入夜前急行軍抵近，直至拂曉才以騎槍齊射衝入營帳村，擊殺、縱火、奪馬，然後立刻退出到十數里外的乾地重整。美軍自己不構築工事，也不占領土著營地，因為一旦留下就等於把後方交給遊擊的騎手。冬季遠征則以分割推進代替追擊：分兵的隊伍分別封住水草與渡口，等候對方營帳在寒季耗盡馬匹與存糧，再在一次總攻中同時攻破數處宿營，德克薩斯帕洛杜羅峽谷的攻擊即屬此類。加特林機槍在這種戰術中處於矛盾位置：它火力足、能封住正面接近的路徑，但重量與人力需求令它難以跟隨連日急行軍，因此只固定在營地與車隊停留處使用，成為遠征軍中少數能在夜裡正面壓制突襲的火力。聯盟方面的戰術是高機動的游擊：白日散在馬背與帳篷之間保持警覺，遠處發現騎兵縱隊即散開，夜晚營地設多層哨戒，營火低埋地坑之下，敵軍接近便滅火分散，敵軍退開再重新生火煮食；作戰時避免與美軍正面交鋒，只在近距離內放箭與射擊後立刻拉開，避免被騎兵追上，只有在被逼入無路可退的谷地時才被迫正面突圍。
tacticsEn: The army had no intention of holding any position in this war, and that fact determined every manoeuvre. The expedition moved in parallel columns across the grasslands, several brigades strong; by day scouting parties searched out the location of the villages, and the columns made a forced march to close on them before nightfall, striking the tent camps at first light with a volley from the carbines, killing, firing the lodges and driving off the ponies, and then withdrawing at once to dry ground a dozen miles away. The Americans built no fieldworks and occupied no native camp, because to stay would have handed their rear to a mounted enemy who never stopped moving. The winter expedition replaced pursuit with divided advance: separate columns sealed the water holes and fords, waited for the opposing camps to exhaust their ponies and stores through the cold season, and then broke several of the winter camps at once in a single general attack, which is what the attack in Palo Duro Canyon in Texas was. The Gatling gun stood in an awkward relation to this manner of war: its fire was heavy enough to seal the approaches head on, but its weight and its appetite for men at the crank made it hard to carry through days of forced marching, so it stayed with the camps and with the wagon trains, and became one of the few means by which the expedition could face a night attack squarely. The confederation's tactics were those of a highly mobile harassment: by day the warriors scattered between horses and lodges and kept a sharp watch, breaking up as soon as a cavalry column was sighted at a distance; at night the camps were guarded in more than one ring, the fires sunk into pits below ground, and doused and scattered when the enemy drew near, to be relit and the cooking resumed once he withdrew. In action they avoided meeting the Americans squarely, loosing arrows and shots at close range and then breaking away at once so as not to be overtaken by mounted troops, and only when cornered in a canyon with no way out were they driven to a frontal charge.
data: 可以核對的數字大致如下。戰爭自一八七四年六月起，到一八七五年底基本結束，主要戰鬥集中在德克薩斯潘漢德北部的斯泰克平原。野牛數量在十九世紀初估計有三千萬至六千萬頭，鐵路與皮革市場刺激下的商業獵殺在 1874 至 1875 年間達到高峰，有估計認為兩年之內被屠殺的野牛超過一千五百萬頭，到一八七〇年代末美國境內的野牛已不足一千頭。一八七四年六月二十七至二十八日臭水溪與野牛谷之戰，第 4 騎兵團由麥肯齊率領約一百二十人，摧毀約一百座帳篷，聚落人口約一千二百至一千四百人；美軍戰報記載斃敵二十七人、傷七十九人，繳獲與擊斃的馬匹超過一千四百匹。一八七四年八月二十六日麥克萊倫溪之戰，麥肯齊率不到一百名騎兵攻擊基奧瓦村落，各家記載的死亡人數在一百至二百五十之間，繳獲馬匹約一千匹、牛皮約一千二百張。一八七五年一月九日清晨，約一千二百名戰士進攻西爾堡，守軍以加特林機槍與三吋野戰炮擊退來犯者。一八七五年三月十三至十四日帕洛杜羅峽谷之戰，第 4 騎兵團攻擊夏延的冬季宿營，俘虜約一千四百人，繳獲馬匹七百餘匹，另有近千匹被擊斃或驅散；美軍自身陣亡四人。距離方面，從奧斯汀到主戰區約五百公里，自堪薩斯城出發約七百公里，遠征軍依靠沿途設站與車隊輸送維持補給。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The war began in June 1874 and was essentially over by the end of 1875, with the fighting concentrated on the Staked Plains in the northern Texas Panhandle. The bison population of the early nineteenth century is estimated at thirty to sixty million head; commercial hunting driven by the railway and the leather market peaked between 1874 and 1875, and it is estimated that more than fifteen million bison were slaughtered in those two years, so that by the late 1870s fewer than a thousand remained in the United States. In the battle of the Stinking Water and Buffalo Wallow of 27 to 28 June 1874, Mackenzie led about one hundred and twenty men of the 4th Cavalry, destroyed some hundred lodges, and struck a village of between twelve hundred and fourteen hundred people; the army report records twenty-seven of the enemy killed and seventy-nine wounded, with more than fourteen hundred ponies captured or killed. At the battle of McClellan Creek on 26 August 1874, Mackenzie attacked a Kiowa village with fewer than one hundred cavalrymen, and the accounts of the enemy dead range from one hundred to two hundred and fifty; about one thousand horses and twelve hundred hides were taken. In the early morning of 9 January 1875 some twelve hundred warriors attacked Fort Sill and were driven off by the garrison's Gatling guns and three-inch field piece. In the attack on the Palo Duro Canyon winter camp on 13 and 14 March 1875, the 4th Cavalry took about fourteen hundred prisoners, captured more than seven hundred ponies and had nearly another thousand killed or scattered; the Americans lost four men. As for distances, the main area of operations lay about five hundred kilometres from Austin and about seven hundred from Kansas City, and the expedition kept itself supplied by establishing depots along the line and relying on its wagon trains.
cause: 打起來的原因可以分三層。最深的一層是野牛的消失：皮貨與牛肉的商業需求，讓德克薩斯與堪薩斯的獵手在三年之內屠空了南部平原的牛群，失去馬匹、帳篷材料與食物的部族在保留地與草原之間走投無路。第二層是保留地制度本身：一八六七年梅迪辛洛奇條約把科曼奇、基奧瓦與南部夏延安置在印第安領土的保留地上，實際上等於把他們趕出出生之地；代理人系統雖供給糧食與牲畜，卻管不住四處遊動的營帳，雙方互不信任。第三層是美軍內部的政策分歧與直接導火線：印第安事務局主張以糧食、牲畜與代理人安撫，軍隊則認為只有摧毀營帳與馬群才能終止襲擊；一八七四年六月麥肯齊在奧斯汀以北搜索到村落並在臭水溪動手，衝突由零星游擊進入全面遠征，同年秋聯盟拒絕進入保留地，遠征軍的規模便被擴大到足以掃過整片斯泰克平原的兵力。代理人托馬斯·墨菲之死則暴露了聯盟對談判毫無信任：他為西爾堡附近幾個聚落配給糧食，但牛群仍被美軍當作戰利品帶走，聯盟頭目認為談判只是拖延，於是戰爭在意志層面上也失去了收束的機會。
causeEn: The reasons for the fighting can be separated into three layers. The deepest was the disappearance of the bison: the commercial demand for hides and beef let hunters in Texas and Kansas empty the herds of the Southern Plains in three years, and the nations, deprived of ponies, of material for tents and of food, found themselves stranded between the reservations and the range. The second layer was the reservation system itself: the Medicine Lodge Treaty of 1867 settled the Comanche, the Kiowa and the Southern Cheyenne on reservations in Indian Territory, which in practice meant driving them from the country of their birth. The agency system gave grain and livestock but could not control camps that moved from place to place, and neither side trusted the other. The third layer was the disagreement of policy inside the United States together with the immediate occasion: the Indian Office held that the tribes could be pacified with food, cattle and agents, while the army held that nothing would end the raids except the destruction of the camps and the ponies. In June 1874 Mackenzie found a village north of Austin and struck it at the Stinking Water, which carried the conflict from scattered raiding into a general expedition; when the confederation refused to enter a reservation that autumn, the expedition was enlarged to a force sufficient to sweep the whole Staked Plains. The death of the agent Thomas Murphy exposed the complete absence of trust in negotiation: he distributed rations to the villages near Fort Sill, yet the cattle were still driven off by the Americans as booty, the chiefs concluded that negotiation was only a delaying tactic, and in the realm of will the war lost any chance of being closed.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果落在牲畜、皮革與人口的結構上，超出戰術層面。第一，戰爭在實質上完成的，是美軍原本沒有能力靠會戰完成的屠殺目標：他們沒有消滅任何一支主力，卻藉著遠征把南部平原的馬群、牛皮與熟肉供應系統逐段摧毀，使聯盟在裝備上無以為續。第二，遠征確立了美軍西部作戰的標準模式：遠程騎兵縱隊、摧毀營地、奪取牲畜、不留駐軍，後來對南方夏延與北部平原的歷次遠征都沿用同一套辦法。第三，加特林機槍這類機關槍在西部戰爭中確立了位置，它們被當成營地防禦與正面封鎖的火門，而不是決定會戰的武器，這一定位延續到一八七〇年代後期對大蘇族的戰爭與一八七七年的尼茲珀斯戰役，第七騎兵團與第四騎兵團都以同樣的架車式加特林機槍作戰。第四，聯盟方面的損失集中在騎兵與馬匹，這是部族社會最難補充的資源；大量被俘者隨後被轉賣到德克薩斯的莊園與牧場充當勞工，使南部分落此後數十年在保留地內的處境更加困窘。第五，戰爭之後草原上的武裝衝突轉入低烈度形式，越界襲擊、偷盜牲畜與酗酒暴力成為保留地警察的主要工作，軍方介入的頻率反而上升；野牛滅絕與保留地制度的組合，最終把西部邊疆問題轉化為二十世紀美國原住民政策的核心課題。
impactEn: The consequences of this war fell on the structure of livestock, hides and population, well beyond the level of tactics. First, what the war actually accomplished was the slaughter that the Americans could not have achieved by any battle: they destroyed no main body of the enemy, but by their marches they broke up the horse herds, the hides and the supply of dried meat on the Southern Plains piece by piece, leaving the confederation without equipment to continue. Second, the expedition set the standard pattern of American warfare in the West: long cavalry columns moving out, camps destroyed, livestock seized, no garrisons left behind, and the later campaigns against the Southern Cheyenne and the northern tribes repeated the same method. Third, the Gatling gun and its kind found their place in western warfare: treated as the covering fire of camp defence and of the frontal approach rather than as a weapon that decided an engagement, a position it kept through the wars against the Sioux in the late 1870s and the Nez Perce campaign of 1877, where the 7th and 4th Cavalry fought with the same carriage-mounted Gatling guns. Fourth, the confederation's losses fell on its mounted warriors and its ponies, the resources a tribal society found hardest to replace, and large numbers of those captured were subsequently sold into the estates and ranches of Texas as labour, which made the position of the southern nations on the reservations far more miserable for the decades that followed. Fifth, after the war armed conflict on the plains dropped to a lower intensity, and crossing the boundary, raiding for livestock and alcohol violence became the main work of the reservation police, so that military intervention became more frequent rather than less; the combination of the extinction of the bison with the reservation system ultimately turned the problem of the western frontier into a central question of Native American policy in the twentieth century.
result: 結果是美軍以摧毀營地與奪取牲畜的辦法，贏得了對南部平原的主動權，卻沒有取得一次可供宣傳的決定性會戰。一八七五年三月帕洛杜羅峽谷的冬季宿營被攻破之後，聯盟的冬季營帳系統被徹底拆散，馬群被大量殺死或驅散，同年秋天以後的記載裡，草原上再也找不到成建制的村落，紅河戰爭的常規戰事到此結束。餘下的是零星的收尾：獨立的營帳在鹽溪一帶存活數年，夸娜·帕克直到一八七八年才接受定居；基奧瓦方面最後能戰的頭目薩坦塔於一八七八年被自己人殺死；美國本土最後一頭野牛也在一八七九年於德克薩斯西部被獵殺。客觀的賬面是這樣的：美軍自身的傷亡極少，代價主要由聯盟承擔，南部平原的三支部族從數十萬人的遊牧社會退縮為保留地內的定居族群，野牛在美國本土瀕臨絕跡；而卡面這件加特林機槍，則在這幾年裡確立了機關槍作為營地與正面防禦骨幹的地位，並在此後十餘年的西部戰爭中，一直留在軍械庫與前線之間。
resultEn: The outcome was that the Americans won the initiative on the Southern Plains by destroying camps and seizing livestock, without winning a single decisive engagement that could be put on a poster. Once the winter camp in Palo Duro Canyon was broken in March 1875, the confederation's winter camp system came apart completely, the herds were killed or scattered in large numbers, and from the autumn of that year onwards the records of the plains contain no more villages of any size: the conventional fighting of the Red River War was over. What remained was the mopping up. Independent bands survived for years in the salt fork country, and Quanah Parker did not accept settlement until 1878; Satanta, the last Kiowa chief able to make war, was killed by his own people in 1878; and the last bison in the United States was shot in western Texas in 1879. The honest ledger runs like this: American casualties were very small and the cost fell mainly on the confederation, the three nations of the Southern Plains drew back from a nomadic society of several hundred thousand into settled ones on the reservations, the bison in the United States came within a hair of extinction, and the Gatling gun on this card, over those same years, established machine guns as the backbone of camp and frontal defence, and stayed for more than a decade afterwards between the arsenal and the front line in the wars of the West.
